status_summary: NHTSA published an interpretive rule on 2025-06-11 limiting what it considers in setting standards, proposed the SAFE Vehicles Rule III on 2025-12-05, and published the final rule on 2026-09-30 (91 FR 61988), which projects a combined fleet average of about 34.9 mpg for model year 2031 and ends inter-manufacturer credit trading for credits earned from model year 2028; its stated effective date is 2026-11-30, so the previously codified standards remain the regulatory text until then, and on 2026-10-02 California and 20 other states, the District of Columbia and five cities petitioned the First Circuit for review. Congress nullified three California waivers, including the Advanced Clean Cars II waiver behind CARB's 2035 phase-out of new ICE car sales, through Congressional Review Act resolutions signed 2025-06-12 (Public Laws 119-15, 119-16, 119-17), which are operative law and are being challenged by California and 10 other states in the Northern District of California with no merits ruling shown. On 2026-06-12 EPA sent four older California waivers to Congress for the same review, including the 2022 reinstatement of the Advanced Clean Cars I waiver, and on 2026-09-02 the D.D.C. preliminarily enjoined EPA from treating those waivers as rules (per law-firm reports), while a Justice Department suit filed in March 2026 arguing Advanced Clean Cars I is preempted by the Energy Policy and Conservation Act has no ruling found. EPA published a final rule on 2026-02-18, effective 2026-04-20, rescinding its vehicle greenhouse gas standards and the 2009 endangerment finding, and no stay or vacatur of the NHTSA rule or the 2025 laws was found as of 2026-10-07.

timeline.event: Secretarial memorandum 'Fixing the CAFE Program', dated 2025-01-28, directs NHTSA to review and reconsider existing fuel economy standards for model year 2022 and later and to propose rescinding or replacing standards as needed to align with administration policy and statutory requirements. Title, date and content are as described in NHTSA's 2025-06-11 interpretive rule (next entry); the linked PDF has no machine-readable text.

NHTSA publishes an interpretive rule, 'Resetting the Corporate Average Fuel Economy Program' (90 FR 24518), stating it will not consider EVs, plug-in hybrid electric operation, or credit trading when setting standards.

President signs three Congressional Review Act resolutions (Public Laws 119-15, 119-16, 119-17) that nullify EPA's approvals of California's Advanced Clean Trucks, Advanced Clean Cars II and Omnibus Low NOx waivers.
NHTSA publishes the proposed SAFE Vehicles Rule III (90 FR 56438) for model years 2022 to 2031; comments close 2026-01-20 with 29,452 comments logged.

EPA publishes a final rule rescinding the 2009 greenhouse gas endangerment finding and all vehicle greenhouse gas standards (91 FR 7686; effective 2026-04-20); petitions for review are due in the D.C. Circuit.

The Justice Department sues the California Air Resources Board in the Eastern District of California (United States v. CARB, No. 2:26-cv-450), seeking a permanent injunction on the ground that Advanced Clean Cars I is preempted by the Energy Policy and Conservation Act (March 2026 per a law-firm alert; exact day not stated, first of month used).

EPA sends four previously granted California vehicle waivers to Congress for review under the Congressional Review Act, including the 2009 greenhouse gas standards waiver, Advanced Clean Cars I and the 2022 reinstatement of that waiver, per a law-firm alert.

In California v. EPA (D.D.C.), Judge Howell grants a preliminary injunction and denies EPA's motion to dismiss, barring EPA from treating the four waiver orders as rules and directing it to restore the status quo before 2026-06-12, per a law-firm alert.
Final SAFE Vehicles Rule III published (91 FR 61988), effective 2026-11-30; includes a technical amendment reflecting Public Law 119-21's change to CAFE civil penalties.

California and 20 other states (including Massachusetts, listed separately as a commonwealth), the District of Columbia and five cities file a petition for review of the SAFE Vehicles Rule III in the First Circuit; it notes the related challenge to the 2025 interpretive rule (California v. NHTSA, Nos. 25-8019 and others) was held in abeyance.

title: Reset CAFE standards to ICE-feasible levels and end California's fuel economy waiver
